title: The Khalsa Demands Grain at Imnabad

blocks.text: At Imnabad the story introduces Jaspat Rai as a revenue officer whose exactions had made the countryside miserable. Hungry Jats left their homes and joined the Singhs because the local administration had bound, beaten, and impoverished the people instead of protecting them.

The Khalsa nevertheless opens with negotiation rather than plunder. Their message is plain: we have no enmity with you, only with the Turks, and the Singhs have long hungered for food after weeks of fighting and flight.

They ask for grain at a fair price and offer to move on without disturbing his district if he behaves reasonably. Jaspat rejects that opening, answers with threats and contempt, and turns what might have remained a bargain over provisions into a challenge that can only end in violence.
